title: Elastic host hedging and preemptive recovery playbook
author: Aisha Reddy
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes a cross-cutting approach for hedging against host preemption (spot/interruptible instances), graceful eviction handling, and automated recovery for inference workloads. It codifies scheduling patterns, runtime responsibilities, observable signals, and safe rollout steps to enable cost-effective use of preemptible capacity while preserving latency and availability SLOs.

Motivation
----------
- Preemptible instances reduce inference unit cost but increase the risk of tail latency and failed requests during eviction windows.
- Teams need a standardized, low-friction pattern to: 1) hedge requests across capacity tiers, 2) detect and mitigate imminent evictions gracefully, and 3) recover without cascading retries or data inconsistency.
- This playbook balances cost and reliability with clear ownership and operational runbooks.

When to apply
-------------
Apply this pattern for services that meet all of the following:
- SLOs allow best-effort degraded throughput with bounded latency degradation (e.g., 99th-percentile latency SLOs <= 2x baseline during brief preemption events).
- Workloads are idempotent or include idempotency tokens that are honored by downstream components.
- The deployment platform supports at least two capacity tiers (non-preemptible and preemptible/spot).

High-level pattern
------------------
1) Tiered routing: route requests using a routing policy that includes at least two capacity tiers: Premium (reserved/dedicated) and Spot (preemptible).
2) Hedging: automatically issue a hedged backup request to Premium if Spot tail latency or eviction-risk grows beyond thresholds.
3) Eviction detection: expose node-level eviction signals (e.g., cloud provider termination-notice header, host-drain-fence file, or agent heartbeat) to the scheduler and the runtime.
4) Graceful drain: on eviction notice, drain KV cache, persist warmup state, and flip incoming Spot requests to Premium for a configured window.
5) Fast fallback: keep a small warm pool of Premium capacity or a prewarmed cold-start snapshot to accept hedged/fallback requests within the latency SLO.

Architecture and responsibilities
--------------------------------
- Edge/Ingress (API gateway): assigns initial request priority and selects routing hints (tier hints, latency budget, idempotency token). Responsible for quick failover to Premium route when backend signals degradation.
- Router/Control Plane: calculates routing weights per tenant based on tenancy, budget, and recent error/latency signals. Keeps a sliding window of Spot health scores.
- Scheduler: places Pods on Spot or Premium pools and subscribes to eviction streams. Implements a preemption-eviction reconciliation loop: when a host reports imminent eviction, scheduler marks affected instances as DRAINING and triggers runtime drain hooks.
- Serving runtime (worker): implements in-flight request quiescing, KV cache snapshotting, and a short-lived accept-only state for idempotency reconciliation. On receive of eviction event, emits telemetry and flips readiness probe to trigger router-level removal.
- Observability: emits eviction_count, preemption_notice_latency_ms, draining_duration_ms, hedged_request_rate, hedged_success_ratio, fallback_latency_p99.

Operational playbook (step-by-step)
----------------------------------
1) Detection
   - If cloud-provider termination-notice is present: mark node as IMMINENT_EVICTION.
   - If scheduler heartbeat jitter > 2x baseline or kernel OOM events spike > 3/min: escalate to suspected host instability.
2) Immediate mitigation (0–5s)
   - Set node readiness=false, route new requests away from node.
   - Emit metric draining_start_ts and start drain timer.
3) Graceful eviction window (5–30s)
   - Complete in-flight tokens with a soft deadline (default 20s). If a request exceeds soft deadline, attempt transparent hedged retry to Premium with same idempotency token.
   - Persist KV cache delta to shared object store (S3/GCS) with strong consistency flag.
   - Snapshot small warmup artifact (model shard indices, tokenizer cache pointers) to accelerate fallback spin-up.
4) Post-eviction reconciliation (30–300s)
   - Confirm node termination and run postmortem trace: collect hedged_request_rate, fallback_latency_p99, and errors by tenant.
   - If fallback latency or error ratio exceeds configured thresholds, scale Premium pool up by configured step.

Key configuration knobs (recommended defaults)
---------------------------------------------
| Key                                    | Default | Notes                                                           |
|----------------------------------------|---------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| hedging.enabled                        | true    | Global toggle for hedged backups                                 |
| hedging.latency_threshold_ms           | 250     | Hedge when queueing or p95 exceeds this for Spot pool           |
| hedging.cooldown_seconds               | 60      | Minimum time between hedging bursts per tenant                   |
| drain.soft_deadline_seconds            | 20      | Soft deadline to finish in-flight tokens during drain           |
| drain.snapshot_target_mb               | 64      | Target size for quick warmup snapshot                           |
| fallback.prewarmed_min_count           | 2       | Minimum Premium instances kept warm per zone/tenant             |
| eviction.signal_grace_seconds          | 30      | Time between eviction notice and host termination (provider)    |

Telemetry and observability requirements
----------------------------------------
Emit the following time-series and traces with these tags: service, team, tenant_id, tier (spot|premium), region.
- eviction.event.count (counter)
- eviction.notice.latency_ms (gauge)
- draining.duration_ms (histogram)
- hedged.request.count (counter) and hedged.request.success_ratio (gauge)
- fallback.latency.p50/p95/p99 (histogram)
- preemption-induced-error.rate (percent)
- cache.snapshot.duration_ms (histogram)

Alerting thresholds (examples)
----------------------------
- P0: fallback.latency.p99 > SLA_threshold for > 5m OR preemption-induced-error.rate > 1% over 10m.
- P1: hedged.request.success_ratio < 95% over 10m.
- P2: eviction.event.count > expected by 3x for 15m (possible cloud-wide issue).

Testing and validation checklist
-------------------------------
1) Chaos test: simulate termination-notice events on 5% of Spot fleet and validate traffic is successfully hedged and fallbacks complete within SLOs.
2) Load test: verify hedging.latency_threshold_ms triggers under controlled queueing and does not cause amplification (hedging storms).
3) Regression test: ensure idempotency tokens are honored and duplicate-effect safeguards are in place.
4) Cost analysis: run a 7-day experiment to compare cost delta with and without hedging enabled per tenant.

Rollout plan
------------
1) Canary (10% of traffic, non-critical tenants): enable hedging.enabled=true and monitor hedged.request.success_ratio and fallback.latency.p99 for 48 hours.
2) Ramp (incremental 25% steps): increment routing weight to Spot in 25% steps, observing cost and error metrics for 24 hours per step.
3) Global enable: enable for all tenants after two successful ramp cycles and verification of stability metrics.
4) Backout: if fallback.latency.p99 exceeds SLO by >2x for >30m, revert to prior routing weights and open an incident.

Owner and escalation
--------------------
- Primary owner: Serving Runtime team (pager: #runtime-oncall).
- Secondary owner: Scheduler team (pager: #scheduler-oncall).
- Escalation policy: page serving runtime after P0 alerts, scheduler if infrastructure-level issues suspected.

Decision record (summary)
------------------------
Title: Adopt hedged backups + graceful snapshotting for preemptible capacity (DR-2025-hedge)
Decision: We will adopt an explicit hedging pattern (best-effort backup requests to Premium) coupled with graceful drain snapshotting instead of relying solely on immediate bulk replication or synchronous mirroring.
Rationale:
- Hedging minimizes user-facing latency impact without requiring all traffic to run on costly Premium capacity.
- Snapshotting small warmup artifacts on drain keeps recovery time low and avoids large replication costs.
Alternatives considered:
- Always-run-on-Premium: too costly for most tenants.
- Synchronous mirroring between Spot and Premium: high write amplification and cost.
Consequences:
- Slight increase in request traffic to Premium during evictions and hedging windows.
- Additional complexity in idempotency and reconciliation logic.

Appendix: example scheduler config (YAML)
--------------------------------------
# Example: Kubernetes annotation / scheduler config
schedulingPolicy: |
  tiers:
    - name: premium
      weight: 20
    - name: spot
      weight: 80
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    latencyThresholdMs: 250
    cooldownSeconds: 60
  drain:
    softDeadlineSeconds: 20
    snapshotTargetMB: 64

CLI snippets and debugging commands
----------------------------------
- Identify draining nodes: kubectl get nodes -l redwood/shard-state=draining -o wide
- Eviction event timeline (example): curl -s http://node-agent:8080/eviction | jq
- Trigger local hedging test: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.internal/v1/test/hedge?tenant=canary" -d '"load:high"'
